Answer: C
Reason: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) is characterized by pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs), which appear as nodular opacities with distinct feeding arteries and draining veins; these lesions create a right-to-left shunt that predisposes patients to paradoxical systemic embolization and cerebral abscesses. Although the provided image appears relatively normal, Option C is the only choice that correctly describes the pathognomonic radiographic features and clinical complications of HHT-associated PAVMs.
